title: Australian runoff loss stayed in four rain history fits, but the Chile contrast changed in six-year drought windows
abstract: We tested whether a reported Australia-Chile drought runoff contrast survives common choices of past rain and uncertainty in the reference fits. We used fixed CAMELS-CL and CAMELS-AUS v2.03 daily data, 42 Chilean and 251 Australian gauges, equal 26-year references and six-year drought windows. Four annual models used current rain and zero, one, three or five years of prior rain. Sampling refitted the reference model and retained shared years and spatial cells. Australian median departures were -13.8 to -16.0% of reference mean runoff; all four conditional 95% intervals were below zero. Chilean estimates ranged from -0.7 to -7.7%. The primary five-year Australia-minus-Chile contrast was -6.7 points [-23.1, +8.8]. The one-year contrast was -13.9 [-31.2, -0.2], but its interval crossed zero with one-year test blocks. Five-year prior-rain slopes were negative at 30 of 42 Chilean gauges, and this model had higher reference validation error than current rain alone. An exploratory nonnegative-slope fit kept a larger Australian loss than in southern Chile across all four memory lengths; the five-year contrast was -15.7 [-31.5, -2.7] at 30 southern Chilean gauges. The whole-Chile contrast was less stable. These results retain the Australian loss, narrow the international comparison, and show why conditioning on past rain changes the question. Short tests, rain-product choice, model limits and few Chilean spatial cells preclude causal attribution or proof of equal losses. The package includes an attributed CC BY 4.0 annual derivative database, exact source hashes, code, sampling draws, figures and independent numerical audits.

display.caption: Six-year drought departures, Australia-minus-Chile contrasts, and reference validation error across four rain history models. Bars show conditional 95% limits with reference refitting, shared weather years and spatial cells. The physical-sign check is exploratory.
Northern and southern Chile give different runoff departures. All groups use the same rain history models. These latitude subsets are not exact snow-regime classes. Bars show conditional 95% limits.
